safety_adjacent_verdict.statement: All three keys PASS. Each was read against the code path that emits it, not only against the English: the Spanish states the same consequence, names the same remedies, and keeps every flag byte-identical. On this evidence the safety-adjacent copy is safe to ship in Spanish. This is a copy verdict: it does not claim any runtime or behavioural test of the approval gate.

per_key.en_promise: this run cannot ask for approval (no terminal attached), so any tool call needing approval will be denied; remedies --control / --yolo / --tools / tool_approval_mode: auto
per_key.es_text: esta ejecución no puede pedir aprobación (no hay terminal conectada), así que cualquier llamada a herramienta que necesite aprobación se denegará
per_key.emit_site: exec_mode.py:1120, reached only when --control, --yolo, a --tools inventory, a declaring profile, a tty and a saved auto approval are all absent
per_key.judgement: PASS. The denial is still stated as a consequence of the missing terminal (the condition the emitter actually checks), not as a blanket rule. All four remedies survive with their flags intact and in the same order, 'every tier' -> 'todos los niveles', and the 'tool_approval_mode: auto answers every call the same way for every run' clause is preserved rather than shortened. No reassurance is added and none is removed: the two-line shape with its two-space indent survives.

per_key.en_promise: --goal sets the objective but does not start work (unlike the TUI's /goal); add a prompt, pipe one on stdin (or '-'), or run a loop with --loop N
per_key.es_text: --goal fija el objetivo pero no inicia trabajo (a diferencia de /goal de la TUI). Añade un prompt, envíalo por stdin (o '-') o ejecuta un bucle con --loop N.
per_key.emit_site: exec_mode.py:1179, when --goal is given with no command and no loop
per_key.judgement: PASS. The refusal still answers the belief that produced it (that --goal also runs, as the TUI's /goal does), which is what the code comment says the message exists for. All three remedies are present and --loop N is byte-identical.

per_key.en_promise: --clear-goal adjusts a run, it does not start one; pair it with --resume SESSION_ID plus a prompt or --loop
per_key.es_text: --clear-goal ajusta una ejecución, no la inicia. Combínalo con --resume SESSION_ID y un prompt o --loop.
per_key.emit_site: exec_mode.py:1174, when --clear-goal is given with no command and no loop
per_key.judgement: PASS. 'ajusta una ejecución, no la inicia' preserves the adjust-versus-start distinction that is the whole point of the message; --resume SESSION_ID is byte-identical and the 'plus a prompt or --loop' pair is intact.

safety_adjacent_verdict.residual_risk: The advisory's accuracy depends on the emitter's branch, not on the translation: if a future change lets a run reach a tty-less start that is not denied, both locales would misdescribe it equally. Recorded so a later reader does not read this verdict as a behaviour test.

findings.detail: 'Waiting on you? lop sessions shows what a run needs' is rendered '¿Algo te espera? lop sessions muestra lo que necesita una ejecución'. The subject flips: the English says a run is waiting on the reader; the Spanish says something awaits the reader. It lands on the same behaviour and is stderr prose with no width budget. Round-1 nit es-w1-C01, not adopted.
findings.remediation: '¿Te está esperando? lop sessions muestra lo que necesita una ejecución'.

findings.detail: The same --tools promise is phrased two ways inside one namespace: 'limita el alcance de esta ejecución a esas herramientas' (approval_advisory) and 'limita a qué puede llegar la ejecución' (exec_epilog). The second is a calque of 'bounds what the run can reach' and reads as translated. Both keep the promise; style only. Round-1 nit es-w1-C02, not adopted.
findings.remediation: Use 'limita el alcance de la ejecución a esas herramientas' in both.

fact_1_label_budget.claim: every settings row label is rendered as truncate_cells(label, 29)
fact_1_label_budget.evidence: settings_view.py:4020 truncate_cells(setting.label, _LABEL_BUDGET); settings_view.py:434 _LABEL_BUDGET = _VALUE_COLUMN(34) - _ROW_INDENT(2) - _MARKER_WIDTH(2) - 1 = 29; truncate_cells cannot wrap (tool_card.py:728-750).
fact_1_label_budget.consequence: Any label over 29 cells is painted cut with a visible ellipsis. Applies to the console rows (settings_io.py:4774-4799, section 'console', always visible) and to the hub and failover rows, not only to the two namespaces the briefing named.

fact_2_wrap_rung.claim_as_briefed: when no rung fits, _wrap_cells(help_text, width, max_lines=2) renders the help across two rows, so the two hub_defaults help strings are acceptable with a narrow-width limit
fact_2_wrap_rung.evidence: The wrap rung is a None entry in the shed ladder and is created only in the bridge_row branches (settings_view.py:4881 for the no-clause case, 4873 region for the clause case). bridge_row is set at settings_view.py:4767 from section == team_bridge.BRIDGE_SECTION, and BRIDGE_SECTION is the literal 'team_bridge' (team_bridge/availability.py:33). The hub rows are section 'hub' (settings_io.py:5120). No None rung exists for them, so _wrap_cells at 4910 is never reached and the ladder's last rung, settings_view.py:4937, applies: truncate_cells(rendered.plain, width) - a marked cut, not a wrap. _wrap_cells' own docstring scopes it to 'the agent-messages explanation only'.
fact_2_wrap_rung.measured: _detail_width() is max(total-2, 24) (settings_view.py:5203), i.e. 98 cells at 100 columns and 78 at 80. agents.help is 113 cells -> truncated at both sizes, whole only from 115 columns. teams.help is 94 -> whole at 100 columns once the key path sheds, truncated at 80.
fact_2_wrap_rung.consequence: The briefing's premise is wrong for this surface; round 1 had it right. agents.help is a real defect (C03 major), not an accepted narrow-width limit. teams.help is a narrow-width limit only (C04 minor).
